content: The Detroit Medical Center (DMC) is a non-profit healthcare corporation based in Detroit, Michigan. It operates nine general and specialty hospitals in the southeastern region of the state. These hospitals include: DMC Children’s Hospital of Michigan, which is the only pediatric Level I trauma center in southeast Michigan. DMC Detroit Receiving Hospital, recognized as Michigan’s first Level I Trauma Center. DMC Harper University Hospital, offering specialized services such as bariatric surgery, cardiology, vascular procedures, neurosurgery, neurology, and kidney and pancreas organ transplants. DMC Huron Valley-Sinai Hospital, located in Oakland County, Michigan. DMC Hutzel Women’s Hospital, specializing in obstetrics, infertility, and gynecology. DMC Kresge Eye Institute, focusing on ophthalmology and cornea transplantation. DMC Michigan Orthopaedic Specialty Hospital, dedicated to orthopedic services. DMC Rehabilitation Institute of Michigan, specializing in rehabilitation medicine and spinal cord injury care. DMC Sinai-Grace Hospital, known for total joint replacement surgery. Additionally, the Karmanos Cancer Institute, while a separate non-profit entity, is closely affiliated with the DMC and is highly regarded for its cancer treatment and research. The DMC has over 2,000 licensed beds, employs more than 12,000 staff members, and has 3,000 affiliated physicians. Many of its hospitals are staffed by physicians from the Wayne State University School of Medicine, the largest single-campus medical school in the United States. The DMC serves as the official healthcare provider for several Detroit-based sports teams, including the Detroit Tigers, Detroit Red Wings, Detroit Pistons, Detroit Shock, and the Detroit Belle Isle Grand Prix. The Detroit Medical Center is fully accredited by the Joint Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Organizations. Notably, DMC Harper University Hospital and DMC Sinai-Grace Hospital have been ranked above the national average in a survey conducted by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) and the Federal Department of Health and Human Services. This survey included data from 4,807 hospitals across the United States, with only 38 hospitals achieving rankings above the national average. These rankings help the public assess hospital performance in treating specific medical conditions, such as heart failure and heart attacks. The DMC is the only health system in Michigan with two hospitals ranked at this level. In 2007, the DMC was named to the nation’s Most Wired list, as determined by the Most Wired Survey and Benchmarking Study. This recognition highlights hospitals that demonstrate superior outcomes in areas such as mortality rates, patient safety, core measures, and average length of stay. The survey emphasizes the use of information technology to improve healthcare quality, customer service, public health, safety, business processes, and workforce management. The DMC has also received the prestigious Best Practices in Infrastructure Management award from Computerworld’s Infrastructure Management World conference. This award recognizes leadership and excellence in the use of infrastructure management technology. The DMC is one of only two organizations nationwide to receive this honor annually. Michael E. Duggan, former Wayne County Executive, has served as the DMC’s President and Chief Executive Officer since January 2004. Emery King, a former WDIV journalist, serves as the DMC’s Communications Director and presents the Emery King Healthcare Video Library on the DMC’s website.
